title: Joint associations between 10-year average residential proximity-based pesticide exposures and cardiometabolic markers among women from an agricultural region - Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology
description: Chronic exposure to multiple agricultural pesticides may influence cardiometabolic disease risk. We examined joint associations between long-term, residential proximity-based exposure to seven pesticide classes and cardiometabolic risk factors among women from an agricultural region using complementary mixture methods. Women participating in the Center for the Health Assessment of Mothers and Children of Salinas Maternal Cognition Study completed anthropometric measurements, blood collection, and interviews in 2022–2024. Using participant-reported addresses and California’s Pesticide Use Reporting database, we estimated average agricultural use (kg/year) of seven pesticide classes within 1 km of homes in the 10 years preceding outcome assessment. We used quantile g-computation (QGCOMP) and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) to estimate joint associations with cardiometabolic risk factors and explore the relative contributions of pesticide classes to joint exposure effects. Participants (n = 459) were 48.4 ± 5.5 years old at outcome assessment. Using QGCOMP, a joint one-quartile increase in pesticide exposures was associated with higher systolic blood pressure (β = 1.82 mm Hg, 95% CI = 0.38, 3.25), higher pulse pressure (β = 1.59 mm Hg, 95% CI = 0.56, 2.63), and lower HDL cholesterol (β = –1.35 mg/dL, 95% CI = –2.61, –0.10; <50 mg/dL or self-report cholesterol medication: RR = 1.12, 95% CI = 1.02, 1.23). BKMR results were generally consistent, with modest nonlinearity for blood pressure (e.g., pulse pressure: p25 to p50: β = 0.32, 95% CrI = –1.65, 2.29; p50 to p75: β = 3.46, 95% CrI = 1.35, 5.57) and elevated risk of low HDL cholesterol (p25 to p50: RR = 1.09, 95% CrI = 1.01, 1.18; p50 to p75: RR = 1.03, 95% CrI = 0.93, 1.13). In exploratory analyses, we found the most consistent agreement for glyphosate herbicide’s contribution to the joint associations with low HDL cholesterol and, to a lesser extent, continuous pulse pressure. Joint associations with other outcomes, including body mass, blood sugar, and inflammatory markers, were null.
